body: It was decided in the core meeting to use `PascalCase` for namespaces. I adjusted the PR accordingly.
Sidenote: all instances of `_FORCE_INLINE_` are redundant here, as `constexpr` implies `inline` for functions.

> Can safely prepend constexpr to these. You're totally right! > Sidenote: all instances of _FORCE_INLINE_ are redundant here, as constexpr implies inline for functions. Technically, just being declared as a member function already implies inline, at least if CLion is right: `FORCE_INLINE` has an additional effect because it will (likely) inline the functions even on `-O0`, when this is not guaranteed by the `inline` keyword. Somebody said they tested compiling `Godot` without all the `FORCE_INLINE` keywords, and noticed substantial performance decreases for dev builds. So they do seem to help somewhat.
Oop, the implementations need to be marked `constexpr` too
I'm not sure if that applies in contexts with `constexpr`, but I suppose it doesn't hurt. Might as well prepend `_FORCE_INLINE_` to these 3 functions too
Oh yeah, that explains the CI problems. I relied on AI and Clion to tell me it wasn't needed and left it out. Good reminder to double check sometimes 😄
They're complex enough that it may be interesting to generate functions for them, e.g. to save space. So I'd rather let the compiler decide and not force inline here.
